display_name: Encoding of the Judicial Selection Committee rules (Basic Law: The Judiciary ss 4, 4A, 4B, 5, 7(4) and the commencement rule of Amendment No. 4), both vintages

run.agent: a Sonnet 5.5 encoder working for the lead of session israel
run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from the lead's brief; the rules read from the page images of the amending instruments

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English. Hebrew is quoted only in comments, copied from the consolidation or the instrument named in the comment; text read from a page image is marked so.

seat: the individual the committee's rules are applied to: a candidate whom the committee chooses or declines to choose as a judge, and a judge whom the committee is asked to remove; the committee, the Minister of Justice, the Knesset and the Court have no seat

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval

other_sources.what: Basic Law: The Judiciary (Amendment No. 4), Sefer HaChukim 3388, 1 April 2025, pp. 434-436: s 1 (s 4(b) replaced, s 4(c) and new s 4(d) to (f)), s 2 (new ss 4A, 4B), s 3 (commencement and application)
other_sources.authority: official publication (the Knesset's PDF of Sefer HaChukim), read from the page images

scope: Encoded: s 4(b) to (f) in two vintages (the text before the 26th Knesset; the text from it, with the case of more than 80 coalition Knesset members), s 4A (the Minister of Justice's decision on a deadlock and the one-month rule), s 4B (the periods when the committee may not elect judges), Amendment No. 4 s 3 (the transitional window), s 5, s 7(4); the cross-references of ss 4A, 4B, 4(e), 4(f) as typed values. Out of scope: every section the amendment did not touch and that is not about the committee (ss 1 to 3, 6, 7(1) to (3) and (5), 8 to 24 except as named); Amendment No. 3 of 2023 (s 15) is not encoded in this run.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source, and no independent tester has run. Every expected value in the tests modules was worked by hand from the Hebrew text of the instrument before it was asserted; a mutation check on scratch copies shows the tests can fail.
